evidence.parameter_check: The damping condition changes damping_scale from the saved 1.323437744597295 to known truth 1.0 while retaining stiffness_scale 1.1273900664775374 and all learned memory ports/time constants. Its comparison control uses those same learned coefficients and the same exact truth forecast-origin state. All six newly evaluated conditions report no execution failures.

conclusion: Among the registered single-block interventions at a common exact truth forecast-origin state, damping replacement alone satisfies the complete train/val recovery, stability and trajectory guards. Replacing only the hidden state does not recover any matched positive window; the all-truth equation succeeds with causal history initialization as well as with exact hidden state. This supports prioritizing damping learning and does not establish a unique cause, eliminate coefficient-initialization interactions, or show that a learned damping correction already works with causal initialization.

next_route.objective: Fit one shared log damping coefficient from complete train trajectory loss while retaining the saved stiffness and memory parameters and the original causal history initializer.
next_route.contract: Freeze the proposed nine-point log-damping grid around the saved coefficient, the plus/minus log(2) range, deterministic bracket and tie rules, at most 24 refinement evaluations, numerical-failure handling, boundary handling and endpoint choice before execution. Freeze the selected coefficient before complete train/val/test reporting; do not expand the search from val or test feedback.
next_route.unresolved_question: Whether a train-selected damping coefficient with causal initialization reproduces the recovery demonstrated by the known-truth intervention. The fit is not authorized by this completed zero-fit scope.
